summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to grow high-quality, ultrathin vanadium dioxide (VO2) films on sapphire substrates at low temperatures (≤150°C). The films exhibit a metal-insulator phase transition near 68°C, which is exploited to tune the refractive index by controlling temperature. The optical properties, including transmittance and reflectance, are measured as a function of temperature to create models of the complex optical refractive index, which can be used for developing tunable refractive index materials.
evidence: To achieve this, we used atomic layer deposition to grow high-quality, low-temperature ( ≤150°C), ultrathin films of vanadium dioxide on sapphire substrates.
